outline.description: Sets out who the parties are, how the premium financing worked, what happened to trigger cancellation, what claims were filed, how the case reached federal court, and the questions presented on appeal.
subtopics: Parties and roles: former insureds Williams and Wright; tort claimant Jenkins; insurer GoAuto; premium finance company APAC
Premium finance agreements and powers of attorney authorizing APAC to cancel upon default
Defaults, ten-day cure notices, and resulting policy cancellations
State-court class action allegations: ineffective cancellation, misrepresentation, breach of good faith and fair dealing
Removal to the Middle District of Louisiana; cross-motions for summary judgment limited to statutory compliance
District court’s ruling granting GoAuto summary judgment and dismissing with prejudice
Issues on appeal: delivery and content of cancellation certification, insurer receipt of request, denial of plaintiffs’ partial summary judgment
Appellate standard of review for summary judgment (de novo) and scope confined to statutory compliance

outline.chapter_title: Louisiana Framework for Cancelling Financed Insurance Policies
outline.description: Explains the governing statute and the strict-adherence jurisprudence that shapes how courts assess finance-company-initiated cancellations.
subtopics: Statutory authority: La. Rev. Stat. § 9:3550(G)(3)(a) allowing a premium finance company to request cancellation after an uncured default
Required finance-company statement certifying four items: valid power of attorney; default not timely cured; ten-day notice to insured with date sent; copies to interested parties
Permissible transmission methods: mail, private carrier, electronic mail
Insurer’s authority upon receipt under § 9:3550(G)(3)(b)(i): may proceed to cancel
Strict adherence requirement and consequences of defects: Delatte v. Lemotte; Eaglin v. Champion Ins. Co.
Purpose of strict compliance: fixing exact cancellation time and preserving minimum cure window (Britten v. Reavis)
How the statutory scheme allocates roles among finance company, insurer, and insured

outline.chapter_title: APAC–GoAuto Cancellation Workflow and the Disputed Procedural Steps
outline.description: Details the actual cancellation process used by APAC and GoAuto and pinpoints where plaintiffs claimed statutory noncompliance.
subtopics: APAC’s ten-day notice to insured after missed payment and opportunity to cure
Automatic email from APAC to GoAuto at the end of the cure period with copy of notice and certification language
Certification content used by APAC: statements that the agreement has a valid power of attorney, is in default not cured, ten-day notice sent to insured, and notice sent to interested parties
GoAuto’s automated receipt and cancellation via a listening web service without human intervention at that moment
Later administrative steps: APAC employee applies signature stamp; physical document handling
Pre-2017 shared filing cabinet; post-2017 hand-delivery to a GoAuto employee for received stamp and filing
Plaintiffs’ challenges: absence of a contemporaneous signature; lack of identified APAC employee; claim that GoAuto never received the request within the meaning of the statute
District court’s alternative rationale referencing private carrier and Huntley analogy (not reached on appeal)

outline.chapter_title: The Fifth Circuit’s Statutory Analysis and Holdings
outline.description: Presents the court’s reasoning on the key statutory terms certifying and receipt, application to the undisputed procedures, and resolution of the parties’ motions.
subtopics: No signature requirement: statute’s text speaks in terms of the company certifying; it does not require a handwritten or electronic signature by a named individual

Comparison to Louisiana appellate cases: KMJ Services and Hodges emphasize a statement certifying compliance; Benitez noted lack of signature among multiple defects but did not make signature dispositive
Strict adherence does not authorize courts to add extra-statutory prerequisites such as a signature
Meaning of receipt: adopting Black’s Law Dictionary definitions of receipt and receive focused on taking possession
Applying receipt to modern systems: GoAuto’s web service that accepts APAC’s email constitutes possession; human involvement is not required before cancellation
Therefore, GoAuto had receipt when its system accepted the email and could cancel immediately afterward
No need to address the district court’s private carrier rationale because email receipt suffices
Consequences: cancellations were effective; misrepresentation and good-faith claims dependent on alleged statutory noncompliance fail
Disposition of motions: affirming summary judgment for GoAuto; plaintiffs’ partial summary judgment properly denied

outline.description: Explains why the court declined to certify questions to the Louisiana Supreme Court and distills operational and doctrinal takeaways.
subtopics: Plaintiffs’ request to certify unresolved statutory-interpretation questions to the Louisiana Supreme Court
Governing approach to certification: Jefferson v. Lead Industries; novelty alone does not justify certification; reserved for compelling reasons
Denial of certification and decision to resolve by applying statutory text and existing Louisiana appellate guidance

Operational takeaways: include all four statutory certifications in the notice; maintain proof-of-mailing records; preserve reliable logs of electronic transmittal and receipt; automated cancellations upon electronic receipt are permissible
Doctrinal takeaway: strict compliance is exacting but does not allow courts to add requirements absent from the statute; statutory terms like receipt encompass modern electronic workflows
Litigation implications: with robust electronic records, statutory-compliance disputes are amenable to summary judgment
